correctness.rationale: The coefficient-norm expansion exactly yields q=1/m-1/(m+tau(m!)²). Uniform positive-real-part bounds handle m>=4; a strict boundary trigonometric inequality plus harmonic minimum handles m=3; convex interpolation between q=0 and q=1 boundary forms handles m=1. For m=2 the imaginary-part integral and Jensen bound prohibit every nonreal zero, while monotonicity on the negative axis gives the unique simple scalar zero exactly above 1-log2. The tau conversion and excluded boundary are checked. No infinite claim relies on finite experiments.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-derivative-order classification of a natural one-jet Hilbert norm deformation of the classical Dirichlet space. The second derivative is the unique order that destroys global kernel zero-freeness, at a sharp universal log2 threshold with a single emerging root. It is a structural boundary rather than a routine one-parameter calculation; it contrasts with multiple-zero regimes for Bergman kernels and provides a precise robustness guarantee for the entire high-order family.
